related_questions.question: Can I get my Experian credit score for free?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, you can get your Experian credit score for free. You can access your Experian credit report and FICO® Score for free through Experian's website. You can also get a free weekly credit report from each of the three major credit bureaus, including Experian, through AnnualCreditReport.com.
Here's how to get your free Experian credit score:

list.snippet: Visit Experian's website.
Navigate to the section for checking your free credit score.
You may need to create an Experian account or log in if you already have one.
You will likely need to provide your last four digits of your Social Security number and other personal information for verification.
You will receive your free FICO® Score 8 and credit report.
Visit AnnualCreditReport.com.
Follow the instructions to request your free credit report from Experian (and other bureaus).
You are entitled to one free credit report every 12 months from each of the three major credit bureaus.
You can also access free weekly credit reports from each bureau, including Experian, until the end of 2026.
Some credit card companies and other financial institutions may also offer free access to your Experian credit score as part of their services.
Check with your credit card provider to see if they offer this service.

text_blocks.snippet: You can access free weekly credit reports from all three major credit bureaus (Experian, Equifax, and TransUnion) through AnnualCreditReport.com. myEquifax: You can get a free monthly Equifax credit report and VantageScore 3.0 through a myEquifax account.

U.S. Bank: Provides free access to your credit score (updated weekly).
Other Banks and Credit Card Companies: Many banks and credit card companies offer free credit scores and monitoring services to their customers.

related_questions.question: Does Experian show your real credit score?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, Experian can show you a score that lenders may use to assess your creditworthiness. Experian is one of the three major credit bureaus that maintains your credit report, and it also provides access to your FICO® Score, which is widely used by lenders. However, it's important to understand that there isn't one single "real" credit score, as different scoring models and versions can produce different scores, even when analyzing the same credit report.

list.title: Experian is a credit bureau:
list.snippet: It collects and maintains your credit history (credit report).

list.title: FICO® Score is a scoring model:
list.snippet: It's a widely used algorithm that uses the information in your credit report to calculate a credit score.

list.title: Experian provides access to your FICO® Score:
list.snippet: When you get your score from Experian, it's often a FICO® Score 8, but lenders may use different FICO® Score versions or even other scoring models.

list.title: Different scores from different sources:
list.snippet: Your scores may vary depending on the scoring model used and the credit bureau providing the report.

list.title: Accuracy depends on data:
list.snippet: The accuracy of your credit score depends on the accuracy of the information in your credit report, which is maintained by the credit bureaus.

list.title: Review your credit report:
list.snippet: It's a good idea to regularly check your credit report for errors and to understand the factors influencing your score, according to Experian.
